ACID: atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability, the guarantees of a database transaction
ACK: acknowledgement, a TCP flag confirming received data
AMQP: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol, the protocol RabbitMQ speaks
AOP: aspect-oriented programming, adding behaviour such as transactions around methods without editing them
ASCII: American standard code for information interchange
AVL: Adelson-Velsky and Landis, the inventors of the self-balancing tree
AWQ: activation-aware weight quantisation, a GPU-oriented way of compressing model weights
BLEU: bilingual evaluation understudy, a score for how many word sequences a text shares with a reference text
BSD: Berkeley Software Distribution, a family of Unix systems
BYOK: bring your own key, users supplying their own API key
CD: continuous delivery or continuous deployment, releasing every change that passes the pipeline
CDC: change data capture, reading a database's change log to stream every committed change
CQRS: command query responsibility segregation, separate models for writing and reading
CSI: Container Storage Interface, how Kubernetes mounts storage and secrets
CSP: content security policy, a header listing which content sources a page may use
CSV: comma-separated values, a plain-text table format
CoT: chain of thought, asking a model to reason step by step before answering
DI: dependency injection, handing a class its dependencies instead of letting it create them
DIP: dependency inversion principle, the D in SOLID
DKIM: DomainKeys Identified Mail, a signature proving an email came from the domain
DRY: don't repeat yourself, keep each piece of knowledge in one place
DTO: data transfer object, a plain shape for data crossing a boundary such as a request body
DWARF: the debugging data format that accompanies ELF binaries
E2E: end to end, a test that drives the whole running application the way a user does
ELK: Elasticsearch, Logstash and Kibana, a log search stack
ESO: External Secrets Operator, syncing secrets from a manager into Kubernetes
FIN: finish, the TCP flag that begins a connection teardown
GBNF: GGML Backus–Naur form, llama.cpp's grammar format for restricting which tokens a model may generate
GDPR: General Data Protection Regulation, the EU and UK law on personal data
GGML: the tensor library underneath llama.cpp; the letters are its author Georgi Gerganov's initials plus ML (machine learning)
GGUF: the model file format used by llama.cpp and Ollama, holding quantised weights
GNU: GNU's Not Unix, the free-software project behind GCC and the core Unix tools
GPTQ: a post-training quantisation method for GPU inference
H2: an in-memory Java database often used in tests
HSTS: HTTP strict transport security, a header requiring HTTPS
IEEE: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, the body behind standards such as IEEE 754 floating point
INI: initialisation file, a simple key=value configuration format
ISO: International Organization for Standardization, the body behind standards such as ISO 8601 dates
ISR: incremental static regeneration, rebuilding static pages after deploy
IV: initialisation vector, a random value that makes encryption of the same message differ
JPMS: Java Platform Module System, the module-info.java modules added in Java 9
JSONB: binary JSON, Postgres's indexed JSON column type
JSONL: JSON Lines, a text format with one complete JSON object per line
KISS: keep it simple, stupid, prefer the simplest solution that meets the requirement
LINQ: Language Integrated Query, C#'s built-in query methods such as Where, Select and Count
LSP: Liskov substitution principle, the L in SOLID
MCP: Model Context Protocol, an open standard for connecting models to tools and data sources
MDC: mapped diagnostic context, per-thread values added to every Java log line
OCP: open/closed principle, the O in SOLID
OWASP: Open Worldwide Application Security Project, which publishes lists of the most common security risks
PII: personally identifiable information, data that identifies a person directly or in combination
PKCE: proof key for code exchange, protecting OAuth logins in apps that can't keep a secret
PKI: public key infrastructure, the system of certificates and authorities
PPM: portable pixmap, a plain-text image format
PRNG: pseudo-random number generator, an algorithm whose 'random' numbers are fixed by its seed
RED: rate, errors, duration, the request-centric monitoring signals
RFC: request for comments, the document series that specifies internet protocols
RLHF: reinforcement learning from human feedback, training a model toward the answers people preferred
RLS: row-level security, database rules limiting which rows a user can see
ROUGE: recall-oriented understudy for gisting evaluation, a family of overlap scores for summaries
RPM: requests per minute, a rate limit on how many calls you may make
RST: reset, the TCP flag that aborts a connection
SAML: Security Assertion Markup Language, an older single sign-on standard
SHA: secure hash algorithm; in Git, the hash identifying a commit
SLA: service level agreement, a contractual reliability promise
SLI: service level indicator, the measured reliability signal
SLO: service level objective, the internal target for an SLI
SMS: short message service, a text message
SOLID: single responsibility, open/closed, Liskov substitution, interface segregation, dependency inversion
SOP: same-origin policy, the browser rule isolating websites from each other
SOPS: Secrets OPerationS, a tool for encrypting secrets inside config files
SPF: Sender Policy Framework, a DNS record listing who may send a domain's email
SPFA: shortest path faster algorithm, a queue-based refinement of Bellman-Ford
SQS: Simple Queue Service, Amazon's managed message queue
SRP: single responsibility principle, the S in SOLID
SSE: server-sent events, a way for a server to stream messages to a client over one HTTP response
SSRF: server-side request forgery, making a server fetch an attacker-chosen URL
SWE: software engineering, or a software engineer
SYN: synchronise, the TCP flag that opens a connection
TAP: a virtual network interface carrying Ethernet frames
TDD: test-driven development, writing a failing test before the code
TGI: Text Generation Inference, Hugging Face's model server
TPM: tokens per minute, a rate limit on how many tokens you may send and receive
TTFT: time to first token, how long until the first piece of a streamed reply arrives
TUN: a virtual network interface carrying IP packets
USSD: unstructured supplementary service data, menus reached by dialling a short code on a phone
UUID: universally unique identifier, a 128-bit ID such as 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000
VCR: videocassette recorder; also a Ruby library that records HTTP calls and replays them in tests
WSGI: web server gateway interface, Python's standard interface between web servers and apps
YAGNI: you aren't gonna need it, don't build for a requirement that hasn't arrived
YAML: YAML Ain't Markup Language, a configuration file format
p50: 50th percentile, the median: half of values are at or below it
p90: 90th percentile: 9 in 10 values are at or below it
p95: 95th percentile: 19 in 20 values are at or below it
p99: 99th percentile: 99 in 100 values are at or below it
p999: 99.9th percentile: 999 in 1,000 values are at or below it
